rules.label: Shell size: exact or next higher
rules.guidance: When selecting the DB shell, match the stated way-count to the catalog exactly. If the exact way-count is not in the catalog, select the NEXT HIGHER way-count, never a lower one. A stated range takes the highest value first.

rules.label: RCCB/RCBO with no stated current: highest available mA
rules.guidance: When a BoQ line describes an RCCB or RCBO but NO leakage current rating is stated anywhere in the context supplied for that row - not in its own description or notes, and not in any ancestor context provided - match the catalog on the other parameters that ARE stated: device type, amp rating, pole configuration. Among the items that match, select the one with the HIGHEST mA rating. If the catalog cannot be matched on those other parameters, leave it BLANK - do not substitute a different amp rating, pole configuration or device type to force a match. When a current IS stated anywhere in the supplied context, match that stated value as normal.

rules.label: ELCB priced as MCB + RCCB
rules.guidance: An ELCB is a combined device and is priced as TWO components: an MCB plus an RCCB. When a BoQ line describes an ELCB, fill two slots - one MCB and one RCCB - both at the stated amp rating and pole configuration. If the ELCB line states a leakage current, apply it to the RCCB; if it states none, R3 applies to the RCCB.

rules.label: Outgoings stated per phase multiply by phase count
rules.guidance: When a BoQ line states a quantity of outgoings or sub-outgoings PER PHASE, the quantity to record is the total across all phases, not the per-phase figure. Multiply the stated per-phase quantity by the number of phases the DB carries: three for a TPN or VTPN DB, one for an SPN DB. For example, a TPN DB described as having 10 Nos of 6A MCB per phase carries 30 in total; the same wording on an SPN DB carries 10. The phase type may be stated anywhere in the context supplied for the row, including in the DB or shell description. Record the multiplied total as the quantity for that slot.

rules.label: Industrial socket paired MCB
rules.guidance: Industrial socket lines are often billed together with the MCB that controls them. Report what the line SAYS about that MCB; the pairing itself is computed downstream. (0) `paired_mcb`: ALWAYS return null for this attribute, even when the text names a specific MCB - the pairing is computed downstream from the facts you report. (1) `mcb_present`: "Yes" only when the text itself NAMES a breaker. The row's `description`, its `notes`, or an `ancestor_chain` entry must contain the word MCB - or an unambiguous equivalent: MCCB, RCBO, RCCB, ELCB, "miniature circuit breaker", "circuit breaker". A word must actually be present: this is a reading test, not a judgement. The following are NOT mentions, and each of them on its own means "No": an incomer or incoming supply; any current or amperage figure, including the socket's own rating; a distribution board, trolley, panel or feeder context; internal wiring; protection implied by the kind of equipment described. When no such word appears, answer "No". If you are unsure, answer "No" - a socket priced without an MCB is corrected in one click, a socket priced with an MCB nobody asked for is invisible. (2) `mcb_amp_a`: if the text states a current specifically for the MCB, use it; otherwise the HIGHEST current stated anywhere in the text (a socket's stated current serves the MCB when no separate MCB current is given). '25/20/16 A' gives 25. Read it from the text itself, never from the `rating` attribute, whose values are ranges that lose the individual figures. Leave it blank only when the text states no current at all. (3) `mcb_pole_stated`: the pole the text states for the MCB (for example 'DP', '4P' meaning FP). Leave it "None" when the text does not state one; do not infer it from the socket's pin count. (4) `mcb_curve_stated`: the curve the text states (C or D). Leave it "None" when none is stated. Steps (2), (3) and (4) describe the MCB only when `mcb_present` is "Yes". When you answered "No", return `mcb_amp_a` blank and `mcb_pole_stated` / `mcb_curve_stated` as "None" - there is no MCB to describe, so there is nothing to read. Deciding (1) is not a consequence of being able to answer (2): a current figure in the text is never evidence that an MCB exists.

rules.label: Junction box face size
rules.guidance: Junction boxes are described as face x face x depth (e.g. '300 mm x 300 x 60 mm'). Record ONLY the face size in mm - the repeated dimension. rules.label: Wire runs, cores, and the number of points in point wiring
rules.guidance:
Point wiring carries three conductors - phase, neutral and earth - so the run
counts across wire 1 and wire 2 add up to three unless the line explicitly
states otherwise.

Read the line as follows.

When a run count is stated, such as 3R x 1.5 sqmm, record it as given: 3 runs,
1 core.

When a size is given with a plain multiplier and no run marker, such as
3 x 1.5 sqmm, the multiplier is the run count: 3 runs, 1 core, 1.5 sqmm.

When only a size is given with no multiplier at all, such as 1.5 sqmm, record
3 runs of 1 core at that size.

In each of those cases, look for a second conductor named separately - an
earth wire, or any further size - before deciding there is only one wire. If
the run counts already total three, there is no second wire and the earth is
one of the runs already counted. But if a size is given with a multiplier of
two and an earth wire is named separately, that is two wires: record the
multiplied size as wire 1 with 2 runs, and the separately named earth as
wire 2 with 1 run.

When the line states two different run counts, such as two runs of 2.5 sqmm
and one run of 1.5 sqmm, record the wire with the higher run count as wire 1
and the lower as wire 2.

When the line gives two sizes with no run counts at all, record the larger
size as wire 1 with 2 runs and the smaller as wire 2 with 1 run.

Record a core count greater than 1 only when the line positively states
multiple cores - 2C, two core, 3 core. A number before the size is a run
count, not a core count.

Also record the NUMBER OF POINTS the line covers. A line reading Set of seven
(7) light points covers 7; Three (3) light point covers 3; a line describing a
single outlet or a single socket on a breaker covers 1. Where the line names
no count at all, record 1. Count the points the line prices, not the number of
such lines in the bill.

rules.label: More than one socket means a 16A switch
rules.guidance:
When a row carries more than one socket, price the switch as 16A regardless
   of the rating stated in the BoQ. This overrides any other rule about switch
   amp rating, including the substitution of a stated 6A switch.

rules.label: A stated 6A switch is priced as 10A
rules.guidance:
No 6A switch exists in the catalog. When a line states a 6A switch, select
   the 10A switch with the same other parameters - the same way count, the same
   indicator option, the same colour. If no 10A variant matches those other
   parameters, leave it blank rather than substituting a different way count or
   indicator option.

rules.label: Switch way count defaults to 1 way
rules.guidance:
Catalog switch items name their way count - 1 WAY or 2 WAY. When the context
   supplied for a row does not state whether a switch is one way or two way,
   select the 1 WAY variant. When the text does state it, match what it says.

rules.label: Cable runs are recorded separately from cores
rules.guidance: A cable line may state a number of parallel runs as well as a core count. Notation such as 2R x 4C x 25 sqmm means two runs of four-core 25 sqmm cable - record 2 as runs and 4 as core. Runs and cores are separate values for cables and must never be multiplied together: the core count identifies which cable in the catalog, and the run count multiplies its price. If a run count is not stated anywhere in the context supplied for the row, record 1. If a core count is not stated, record 1.
